A letter is a small, fussy document: the recipient's address in the right place, a subject line with the right label, an opening and a closing, and often a letterhead and a signature.

`letter` is a Quarto format that takes those as front matter and lays them out, so the body of the letter is the only thing left to write.

## Starting a letter

```bash
quarto use template {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This installs the format and writes a starting document.

## Adding it to a document you already have

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

## Quick start

```yaml
format:
  letter-pdf:
    address:
      - Director Doe & Co
      - 35 Anthony Road
      - Newport
      - Ipswich IP3 5RT
    subject: collaboration
    opening: "Dear Sir or Madam,"
    closing: "Yours Faithfully,"
```

```bash
quarto render letter.qmd --to letter-pdf
```

Only `address` is required; everything else is left out when it is not given.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for a bilingual letter and one with a letterhead.

## Where it works

PDF, through LaTeX.

HTML will follow once Paged.js is available in [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

A rendered letter is attached to each [release](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-letter/releases), since this site is HTML and cannot show one.
